messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D top-down city-block car chase game.

## Requirements
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px) and read only the latest.

## Decisions
- Implemented a standalone HTML5 Canvas game with keyboard and touch controls, a single city block, cash-drop objectives, police pursuit, car damage, and a garage escape goal.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the game in `index.html`, including its visuals, HUD, responsive layout, and gameplay loop.
- Extracted the inline script and verified syntax with `node --check /tmp/opencode/game.js`.
- Captured and inspected an initial 1280×800 PNG using system Chromium.

### Active
- Finish browser-based verification and address any gameplay or visual issues found.

### Blocked
- The initial `playwright-cli open` failed because Playwright’s Chromium browser was missing; `playwright-cli install-browser chromium` subsequently completed, but a new Playwright run has not yet been done.
- The initial development server command timed out and is no longer serving; restart it before browser verification.

## Next Move
1. Restart a local server for `index.html`.
2. Run Playwright in the browser now installed; exercise start, driving, pickups, and police chase.
3. Save a small JPEG screenshot and inspect only that latest image.
4. Fix any issues, then summarize assumptions and verification results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entire game implementation.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- The initial PNG screenshot was saved at `/tmp/opencode/game.png` and inspected; it was not converted to JPEG.
- Playwright browser installation succeeded with `playwright-cli install-browser chromium`.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D top-down city-block car chase game in `index.html`.

## Requirements
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; note them briefly when finished.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px) and inspect only the latest.

## Decisions
- Implemented a standalone HTML5 Canvas game with keyboard and touch controls, cash-drop objectives, police pursuit, car damage, and a garage escape goal.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added game visuals, HUD, responsive layout, and gameplay code to `index.html`.
- Installed Playwright Chromium and started a local server; `http://localhost:3002/` responds with HTTP 200.
- `node --check /tmp/opencode/game.js` passed for an earlier extracted script.

### Active
- Repair `index.html`: Playwright’s page snapshot shows JavaScript source rendered as page text, and `index.html` has duplicated game code appended after `</html>`.
- Recheck syntax and browser behavior after the repair.

### Blocked
- Browser verification of gameplay is pending until the malformed HTML/script is fixed.

## Next Move
1. Inspect and repair `index.html`, removing the duplicate code after `</html>` and confirming the intended script is inside the document.
2. Run `node --check` on the extracted script and use Playwright to test starting and driving.
3. Save and inspect a latest JPEG screenshot at a viewport no wider than 1280px; address any remaining issues.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entire game implementation; currently includes duplicated code after the document close.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Playwright opened `http://localhost:3002/`; its snapshot included a long block of JavaScript as visible page text. The only reported console error was a missing `/favicon.ico` (404).
